wgr003CrossCheck.question: Does the worker boot require its own SUPABASE_URL (distinct from NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL), and does a missing value hard-exit the worker?
wgr003CrossCheck.answer: Yes, confirmed by direct code read: worker/index.ts:17-43 validateEnv() checks process.env.SUPABASE_URL (not NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL -- a completely separate env var the Next.js web app uses), alongside SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and WORKER_ID. If any of the four is falsy, it logs '[Worker] Fatal: missing required env vars: ...' and calls process.exit(1) synchronously, before any processor (including StreamServer) is constructed.
wgr003CrossCheck.railwayProdStatus: Reid confirmed SUPABASE_URL is present in Railway production. This audit did not independently read the variable's live value in Railway's dashboard/CLI (that would require exposing a production secret) -- but this session's boot-log evidence goes a step further than presence-confirmation: the live boot log (test-evidence/pt-08/railway-boot-window.json) shows the worker reaching '[Worker] AutoApply Worker started' and every processor's own 'Starting' line, all of which are only reachable if validateEnv() already returned successfully (module-level code that runs before any of main()'s awaited calls). This is direct, live proof that all four required env vars, including SUPABASE_URL, are genuinely set and truthy in the current Railway production deployment -- not just reported present by Reid.
wgr003CrossCheck.registerCrossReference: WGR-003 (test-evidence/_register/WIRING_GAP_REGISTER.md) already documents the local-.env.local absence of SUPABASE_URL and the resulting hard-exit risk. This PT-08 pass adds the missing production-side confirmation that WGR-003 explicitly flagged as unresolved ('worth Reid confirming these are genuinely unset in Vercel/Railway production too') -- for SUPABASE_URL specifically, production is confirmed fine by live evidence, not just verbal confirmation. See the Edit made to WGR-003's row in this session.
